definition.def: Coordination means organizing the activities of two or more groups so that they work together efficiently and know what the others are doing.
examples: ...the lack of coordination between the civilian and military authorities.

definition.def: If you do something in co-ordination with someone else, you both organize your activities so that you work together efficiently.
examples: ...operating either in coordination with federal troops or alone.

definition.def: Coordination is the ability to use the different parts of your body together efficiently.

examples.sentence: International groups such as the Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee have developed guidelines on space sustainability.
This interpersonal coordination underlies a wide array of human activities, ranging from more complicated ones like ballroom dancing to simply walking or talking with friends.

In conversations, interpersonal coordination is found when people adjust the duration of their utterances and their speech rate to one another so that they can enable turn-taking to occur, without talking over each other or experiencing awkward silences.

There is a sense among both government officials and residents that the speed, dedication, and coordination of firefighters from several states and jurisdictions are resulting in greater efficiency than in past 'siege fire' situations.
PE teachers help the development of coordination, balance, posture and flexibility with things like simple catching and throwing skills.
